# Parallel vocabulary for transform_cards.py
#
# Format: one term per line. Multi-word terms on a single line, separated by
# single spaces. Lines starting with '#' are comments. Blank lines are ignored.
# All terms are matched case-insensitively.
#
# Two sections, separated by a section header:
#   [tokens]      — words/phrases that *signal* a parallel. A run of tokens
#                   (and optional qualifiers) at the end of the subset string
#                   triggers the split. At least one token must be present in
#                   the trailing run for a split to happen.
#   [qualifiers]  — words/phrases that may *appear inside* a parallel run but
#                   are not enough on their own. They glue tokens together
#                   without triggering a split by themselves.
#
# When the heuristic guesses wrong, the fix is usually to add a missing term
# here — no Python edits needed.

[tokens]

# 'rookie cup team' was tested as a multi-word parallel but caused real
# inserts like "Topps All-Star Rookie Cup Team" to be mis-split. Removed.

[qualifiers]

# Glue words / qualifiers — appear inside parallel runs but never trigger a
# split on their own. Deliberately *not* listed here: insert-name nouns like
# "autographs" (plural — belongs in the subset, e.g. "Chrome Update
# Autographs") and generic words like "edition"/"parallel".
die
cut
die-cut
numbered
shock
border
stripes
&
and
of
the
sp
ssp
sps
x
to

# Discovered from CardTemplate DB. Singular "autograph" / "auto" / "on-card"
# appear *inside* parallels (e.g. "(Authentic On-Card Autograph)"); plural
# "Autographs" stays out of the vocab so insert names like "Chrome Update
# Autographs" still keep their last word.
on-card
autograph
auto
holiday
w/
etch
art
rare
illustration
status
basketball
no
parallel
-
variation
spanish
# 'edition', 'super', 'special', 'premium', 'international', 'collection',
# 'double', 'points' all tested but they appear in CSV insert names too
# often to safely treat as qualifiers (e.g. "Xtra Points <color>", "Special
# Edition <color>"). Left out — DB rows with these in parallels stay in
# the residual mismatch bucket.
